clips.title: The story
paras: King Magni Bronzebeard has commissioned a monument to Sully Balloo, a dwarven soldier who perished defending the Thandol Span. To honor the fallen warrior with enduring dignity, Grand Mason Marblesten dispatches travelers to Hillsbrad to retrieve pristine Alterac Granite.

When King Magni Bronzebeard decided that fallen soldier Sully Balloo deserved a lasting memorial, the task fell directly to Ironforge's finest craftsman, Grand Mason Marblesten. Balloo lost his life during the disaster at the Thandol Span, a vital artery connecting the dwarven lands to northern kingdoms that has suffered brutal attacks by Dark Iron saboteurs. To Marblesten, fulfilling the king's royal decree means creating a sculpture that will withstand both time and war, ensuring that dwarven sacrifice is neither overlooked nor forgotten in the Great Forge.

A master dwarven mason will not settle for ordinary quarry rock for a king's project. Marblesten insists that Sully Balloo's likeness can only be captured in Alterac Granite, a dense, resilient stone prized for its durability and clean texture. The challenge lies in securing it: the best deposits lie around Darrow Hill within the contested foothills of Hillsbrad. Venturing deep into the troubled north is dangerous, but dwarven stonework demands materials worthy of the heroism they commemorate.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: So our good King would like a memorial built in honor of a soldier named Sully Balloo? And you say the poor chap died during the Thandol Span tragedy?
Bah, will there ever be peace on Azeroth?

Nonetheless, any commission from the King is of utmost importance. To build a truly epic and lasting piece I want to work with one of the finest stones available. Travel to Darrow Hill in Hillsbrad and gather for me some Alterac Granite.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Friend, friend, friend! Tell me you have enough Alterac Granite for me to begin my masterpiece in honor of Sully Balloo.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Perfect! Better than I could have imagined!
And I have quite an imagination you know...
